title: Burgess Owens highlights education hearings and wildfire research bill for Utah - West SLC News
text:
Rep. Burgess Owens, U.S. Congressman representing Utah’s 4th district since 2021, posted a series of updates on December 3, 2025, highlighting his involvement in education policy and wildfire research legislation.
In a post at 18:58 UTC, Owens announced his participation in a congressional hearing focused on student privacy laws. He wrote, “I’m joining @EdWorkforceCmte for a K–12 hearing on FERPA and PPRA – the laws that safeguard student education records and protect parental rights. Tune in at 2 PM ET.”
Later that day at 19:44 UTC, Owens expressed support for new federal wildfire research initiatives benefiting Utah. He stated, “Proud to support @RepMikeKennedy’s Utah Wildfire Research Institute Act to expand the federal wildfire research network to include Utah, giving our state’s scientists, firefighters, and land managers the tools and partnerships they need to better prevent, manage, and fight”.
At 20:23 UTC on the same day, Owens commented on issues of transparency and political balance in taxpayer-funded scholarship programs during a higher education subcommittee hearing. He posted, “The Truman Scholarship is funded by taxpayers – yet conservatives are being selected at a 14:1 disadvantage, and basic transparency is nowhere to be found. Today’s @EdWorkforceCmte Higher Ed subcommittee hearing made it clear: taxpayer-funded programs must serve ALL Americans.”
Owens’ remarks come as he continues his tenure representing Utah’s 4th District after succeeding Ben McAdams in Congress in 2021. Born in Columbus, Ohio in 1951 and currently residing in Salt Lake City at age 71, Owens holds a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Miami (1974).
